title: On-call handoff + temp runbook (Riley Thompson)
body:
Shift summary - 2026-03-03 -> 2026-03-04

TL;DR:
- Quiet evening overall. Two noisy alert storms (autoscaler thrash and model-cache evictions). Both mitigated with temporary config changes and follow-up tickets opened.
- No customer-facing outages. Minor increased tail latency for multi-seq gen endpoints during autoscaler thrash.

Active items to pick up:
- OPS-1289 (autoscaler: reduce sensitivity) - assigned to Maya, P1 for this week's run.
- Follow-up for model cache tuning (notes below) - Samir to validate quantized-model eviction policy.
- Temp script for clearing bad cache keys (see quick commands) - needs cleanup and adding to tools repo.

Incidents and current status:
1) Autoscaler thrash — 2026-03-03 19:12-20:05 UTC
   - Symptoms: rapid scale-up/scale-downs on dedicated pools (dp-us-east-1a) causing increased pod churn and transient queueing. Alerts: AS-HighCPU flapping, PoolScale-Failure 5xx spikes.
   - Mitigation performed: increased cool-down to 180s and bumped min_replicas from 2->3 for dp-us-east-1a via temporary policy override.
   - Temporary action ID: JIRA-OPS-1289.
   - Next steps: Roll this change into autoscaler config if post-change metrics look good for 48h. Add a canary to ensure not over-provisioning.

2) Model cache eviction noise — 2026-03-03 21:30 UTC ongoing
   - Symptoms: frequent evictions observed for 7B-quant models leading to increased cold-start tokens and latency spikes for specific routes (chat-moderation, long-context-gen).
   - Hypothesis: batcher + prefix cache sizing mismatch under increased multi-request workloads.
   - Mitigation performed: temporarily raised cache_size for 7B-quant class to 22GB (was 16GB) on a single pool to validate. Also disabled aggressive LRU trimming during peak windows.
   - Notes: this is a stop-gap; need to instrument better telemetry for per-model eviction reasons.
   - Follow-up: Create dashboard panel for per-model eviction rate and average cold-start token count (ticket created).

Routine checks completed during shift:
- Verified all SLO dashboards green except tail-latency for gen-llm routes (P95 up ~30ms).
- Spot-checked dedicated pool utilization, no out-of-disk or OOMs.
- Confirmed backup job for config-store ran at 04:10 UTC.
- Cleared two stale alerts that were known noise (related to telemetry exporter restarts).

Temporary procedures (draft) - add to runbook once validated:
- If autoscaler AS-HighCPU starts flapping (3+ scale events in 10m):
  1) Check pool events: kubectl -n inference get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler -o wide
  2) Inspect metrics: grafana dashboard -> "Autoscaler / Pool dp-us-east-1a". Look for CPU spike vs queue length.
  3) If flapping and CPU oscillation present, set temporary cooldown to 180s and min_replicas +1 for affected pool:
     - CLI: redwoodctl pools update dp-us-east-1a --min-replicas 3 --cooldown 180 --reason "oncall temp override"
  4) Post a note in #sre-oncall and open/annotate JIRA-OPS-1289.
  5) Monitor for 30-60m, then revert if stable after consulting oncall lead.

- If model-cache evictions spike for a model class (evictions > 50/min for >5m):
  1) Identify model class from eviction logs: curl http://telemetry.internal/ejections?since=5m
  2) Apply temporary increase to model cache size for one pool to test: redwoodctl cache set --pool dp-us-east-1a --model-class 7B-quant --size-gb 22
  3) Disable LRU trimming window: redwoodctl cache tune --pool dp-us-east-1a --lru-trim-window 0
  4) Create a short-lived traffic shadow to a canary pool if possible.
  5) Create ticket with dumps (eviction logs + sample request ids) and tag eng-serving-runtime.

Quick commands (notes-to-self):
- Check live alerts: rgrep "Alert" /var/log/oncall/alerts.log | tail -n 100
- Scale override: redwoodctl pools update <pool> --min-replicas <n> --cooldown <s> --reason "oncall temp override"
- Revert override: redwoodctl pools reset-overrides <pool>
- Flush specific cache key (temporary): redwoodctl cache purge --pool <pool> --key "model:7b:abcd1234"
- Dump recent eviction events: redwoodctl cache events --since 30m --json > /tmp/evictions.json

Escalation contacts (order):
1) Oncall SRE lead: Maya Singh (slack @maya)
2) Serving runtime owner: Arjun Desai (slack @arjun)
3) Platform infra: Samir Ali (pager)
4) Eng manager oncall: Priya Menon (email)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Need long-term autoscaler tuning plan: document thresholds and rationale (assign to eng-sre working group).
- Validate whether cache eviction root cause is material fragmentation or batching behavior; add more per-sequence telemetry.
- Add runbook section for function/tool-calling failure modes (noticed one rate-limit warning earlier; not investigated tonight).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a "safety cap" metric that prevents autoscaler from scaling below a baseline when eviction rate high.
- Ideas for telemetry: attach per-request cold-start flag in tracing so we can slice by model + customer.

Related links and references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Autoscaler+Design+Notes
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-1289
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1677629000000
- PR for cache tuning: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/72

End of handoff.

If you pick this up, ping me on slack @riley if you want a quick context walk-through.

---
Draft metadata (for later conversion to shared runbook):
- Severity mapping for autoscaler alerts (high/med/low)
- Standardized temp-override CLI usage and tagging format
- How long to leave temp overrides before escalation (recommended 48h)
- Owner assignment heuristics

(END)
